title: Effect of direct adrenaline infusion into isolated rat heart on the induction of ventricular tachyarrhythmias☆
author: Aksu, Hložková, et al.
materials: Rats were anaesthetised under a Vetequip inhalation anesthetic system and vaporizer (Livermore, CA, USA) with 2.5 % isoflurane. Anaesthesia continued until attenuation of loss of retinal reflexes and pedal reflexes (toe pinch). Later, 0.5 ml of heparin (5000 IU/ml, Zentiva, Czechia) was administered intraperitoneally. Later the rats were decapitated. Hearts excised from the body, placed into ice-cold saline immediately. The cannula inserted to the aorta and positioned between the brachiocephalic artery and the left common carotid artery. After cannulation, truncus pulmonalis is pierced to provide an outflow from the right ventricle. Langendorff isolated perfused heart IH-5 core system (Harvard Apparatus, Massachusetts, USA) used in this study for the perfusion of the hearts. Krebs solution used as a perfusate in the composition of (mmol/L) d-glucose 5.55; KCl 4.70; KH2PO4 1.18; MgSO4 x 7H2O 1.1765; NaCl 118.00; NaHCO3 24.88; Na-pyruvate 2.00 and CaCl2 2.52. The chemicals were obtained from Merck Kga, Lach:Ner and Penta Chemicals. Before the experiment, the solution was saturated with 95 % O2 and 5 % CO2 (Linde Gas). A benchtop pH meter (Orion Star A111, Thermo Scientific) and pH electrode (Orion Triode Refillable Electrode, Thermo Scientific) were used to measure pH. Calibration of pH done with three different calibration solutions (pH 4.006 buffer, pH 6.865 buffer, pH 9.180 buffer, Thermo Scientific). After calibration of the electrode, pH was continuously monitored to keep it at 7.4 and maintained by adding 1 mol/l HCl or 1 mol/l NaOH (Merck) into the solution. Temperature of the system set to 37.6 °C using a circulating bath at (Optima TX150). Constant perfusion pressure set to 80 mmHg (Perfusion Pressure Control with Starling Resistor for IH-5, Harvard Apparatus). Backflow from the aortic block to the reservoir was provided during all experiment protocols in all hearts by using the servo controller (Hugo Sachs Elektronik, Harvard Apparatus) in direct mode. LAD artery was ligated with a monofil suture (USP 3–0) and a silicone tubing occluded on the artery using a micro-bulldog clamp. Ischemic zone confirmed by the injection of methylene blue (MB) (Roth Chemicals, Germany), after the occlusion. MB dissolved in saline and injected to the aortic block of Langendorff apparatus. After injection, MB dispersed in Krebs solution, perfusated to the isolated heart and washed out. The Ischemic zone was approved by the observation of pink- pale tissue, while the non-ischemic zone tissue was in dark blue colour. Ischemia was followed by 5 mins of reperfusion by simply removing the silicon tubing (Fig. 2)Fig. 2Preparation of left anterior descending artery occlusion (1a), application of occlusion (1b) and removal of occlusion (1c) on isolated beating rat heart in the Langendorff apparatus.Fig 2

steps.title: Anesthetize and heparinize rats
steps.instruction: Induce anesthesia with 2.5 % isoflurane using a Vetequip inhalation system (Livermore, CA, USA) until loss of retinal and pedal reflexes, then inject 0.5 ml heparin (5000 IU ml⁻¹, Zentiva, Czechia) intraperitoneally and decapitate the animal.

steps.title: Excise heart and place on ice
steps.instruction: Rapidly remove the heart, immerse it in ice‑cold saline, and keep it chilled until cannulation.

steps.title: Cannulate aorta and ventricle
steps.instruction: Insert a cannula into the aorta between the brachiocephalic artery and the left common carotid artery; pierce the truncus pulmonalis to allow right‑ventricular outflow.

steps.title: Prepare Krebs perfusate
steps.instruction: Make Krebs solution (mmol L⁻¹): d‑glucose 5.55; KCl 4.70; KH₂PO₄ 1.18; MgSO₄·7H₂O 1.1765; NaCl 118.00; NaHCO₃ 24.88; Na‑pyruvate 2.00; CaCl₂ 2.52 (chemicals from Merck Kga, Lach:Ner and Penta Chemicals). Saturate with 95 % O₂ / 5 % CO₂ (Linde Gas), calibrate a pH electrode (Orion Star A111 with Orion Triode Refillable Electrode, Thermo Scientific) using buffers pH 4.006, 6.865 and 9.180, and adjust continuously to pH 7.4 with 1 mol L⁻¹ HCl or 1 mol L⁻¹ NaOH (Merck).

steps.title: Set perfusion system parameters
steps.instruction: Mount the heart on the Langendorff IH‑5 core system (Harvard Apparatus, MA, USA), set the circulating bath (Optima TX150) to 37.6 °C, maintain constant perfusion pressure at 80 mmHg (Starling Resistor, Harvard Apparatus), and enable backflow to the reservoir via the servo controller (Hugo Sachs Elektronik, Harvard Apparatus) in direct mode.

steps.title: Start perfusion and stabilize heart
steps.instruction: Begin perfusion with the prepared Krebs solution, allow the heart to equilibrate for the protocol‑specific stabilization period (Protocol A: 15 min; Protocol B: 10 min) while continuously monitoring temperature, pressure and pH.

steps.title: Ligate LAD artery and occlude
steps.instruction: Tie the left anterior descending (LAD) artery with a USP 3‑0 monofilament suture, place a silicone tubing over the artery, and secure with a micro‑bulldog clamp to create regional ischemia.

steps.title: Confirm ischemic zone with methylene blue
steps.instruction: Dissolve methylene blue (Roth Chemicals, Germany) in saline, inject into the aortic block of the Langendorff apparatus, allow dispersion in the Krebs solution, and observe pink‑pale tissue in the ischemic region versus dark‑blue non‑ischemic tissue.

steps.title: Apply ischemia and adrenaline infusion
steps.instruction: Maintain regional ischemia for the protocol‑specific duration (Protocol A: 40 min; Protocol B: 10 min). In adrenaline groups, infuse adrenaline continuously during the last 5 min of ischemia and the subsequent 5 min of reperfusion; control groups receive no adrenaline.

steps.title: Reperfuse heart
steps.instruction: After the ischemic interval, remove the silicone tubing to allow reperfusion for 5 min.

steps.title: Record surface ECG throughout experiment
steps.instruction: Attach four standard “limb” electrodes (Input Boxes for Multi‑ECG, Harvard Apparatus) plus “hand” electrodes on the left and right ventricular walls and “hindlimb” electrodes under the apex using K‑H solution; ensure consistent placement to avoid artefacts. Begin ECG acquisition when the heart is hung in the system, using Isoheart v2.0 software (Hugo Sachs Elektronik, Germany) and capture strips from leads I, III, aVF and aVR in 2.048‑second intervals.

steps.title: Measure QRS and QT intervals
steps.instruction: Open the captured ECG strips in ImageJ (Wisconsin, USA). Set the global scale: 1868 pixels = 2.048 ms, pixel aspect ratio = 1.0, yielding 0.9121 pixels ms⁻¹. Apply this conversion to all strips. Measure the QRS interval from the start of the Q wave to the end of the S wave, and the QT interval from the start of the Q wave to the end of the T wave, using data from the stabilization and reperfusion periods (excluding any 5‑min reperfusion segment containing ventricular tachyarrhythmias).
